page.title: gscandelari-ecommerce-api — Microservices E-commerce API
hero.desc: A complete e-commerce REST backend — catalog, orders, real payments (test mode) via Stripe, cancellation and refunds, e-mail notifications — built as a microservices architecture on Firebase, with automated tests and continuous deployment.
about.subtitle: What this is
about.p1: This is a portfolio project — a real e-commerce API with complete business rules (not a toy CRUD): stock decremented transactionally, an order state machine, real payments in Stripe test mode confirmed via signed webhook, deliberate cancellation and refund flows, and e-mail notifications to the customer.
about.p2: Built incrementally with TDD (tests written before implementation), test coverage above 70% in every service, mandatory CI on every change, and manual (never automatic) deploys to the real Firebase project, always in test/sandbox mode — this project never processes real money.
about.p3: The architecture is made up of three independent microservices behind an API Gateway, with internal communication authenticated via Google ID tokens — a deliberate choice to demonstrate command of distributed-systems patterns, not just CRUD.
arch.subtitle: Microservices architecture
arch.gateway.title: API Gateway
arch.gateway.desc: Firebase Hosting as the single entry point, routing each path to the right service.
arch.orders.title: Orders
arch.orders.desc: Exclusive owner of products and orders. Transactional stock, state machine, cancellation.
arch.payments.title: Payments
arch.payments.desc: All Stripe integration lives here: PaymentIntent, signed webhook, refunds.
arch.notifications.title: Notifications
arch.notifications.desc: Reacts to order status changes via a Firestore Trigger and sends e-mail — no public HTTP route.
arch.note: Orders and Payments communicate synchronously over internal HTTP, authenticated with a Google-signed ID token — each service runs under its own dedicated runtime service account, with the minimum IAM permissions required. Notifications is asynchronous and best-effort: an e-mail failure never reverts an order transition that already happened. See full diagram →
features.subtitle: What the API does
feature1.title: Product Catalog
feature1.desc: Full CRUD, admin-only writes, Zod validation.
feature2.title: Orders & Stock
feature2.desc: Creation with transactional stock decrement and a complete state machine.
feature3.title: Real Payments (test mode)
feature3.desc: A Stripe PaymentIntent per order, confirmed via signed webhook, idempotent.
feature4.title: Cancellation & Refunds
feature4.desc: Cancellation by Customer or Admin depending on order state; refunds always manual and deliberate.
feature5.title: E-mail Notifications
feature5.desc: E-mail to the customer on order confirmation/cancellation — best-effort, never blocking.
feature6.title: Authentication & Authorization
feature6.desc: Firebase Auth with an admin custom claim — the real source of truth lives in the backend.
